newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS-Creditanstalt set for record year.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Creditanstalt set for record year.

text.p: Creditanstalt, reporting a 70 percent surge in group net profit in the first half, said on Friday it expected to turn in a significantly higher net profit in 1997 for the fifth year in a row.

Investors welcomed the robust earnings and bullish forecast, sending the ordinary shares up three schillings to 850 in an overall limp Vienna market, and the preference shares up 0.6 schillings to 569.5 by late trade.

The bank said its strong international operations and trading profits helped to boost its six-month net profit to a record 2.2 billion schillings ($170.5 million) from 1.3 billion in the year-ago period.

"For 1997 -- even without the effects of realised gains -- management expects a substantial increase in profit after taxes for the fifth year in succession, primarily as a result of the continued decline in provisioning requirements for credit risks," the bank said in a statement.
Creditanstalt's book gains from sales of equity investments reached over two billion schillings in the first half.

Alarich Fenyves, director of the board, told journalists it was too early to comment on the size of the dividend this year but said: "It's obvious that substantially higher earnings would increase room for movement on the upside."
Operating profit surged 38 percent to 4.2 billion in the first half as operating income reached 10.855 billion and operating expenses rose 10 percent to 6.649 billion.
Net profit on trading activities doubled to 1.8 billion schillings from 900 million, while income from securities and investments climbed to 1.2 billion schillings from 350 million.

"These are very strong results. Certainly better than we had been looking for and will definitely lead us to raise our estimates for Bank Austria unless some negative surprises emerge from its earnings -- which we don't expect," said Matthew Czepliewicz, analyst at Salomon Brothers in London.

Market leader Bank Austria, which in January acquired two thirds of Creditanstalt's voting shares from the Republic of Austria for 17.2 billion schillings, will report consolidated results of the Bank Austria/Creditanstalt group on Monday.
Creditanstalt said its foreign branches and leading subsidiaries in central and eastern Europe reported new record profits for the first half of 1997.

Its investment banking arm CAIB also notched up its best results to date with group operating income rising more than threefold to 905 million schillings due to strong performances above all in Russia, followed by Hungary and Poland.

Creditanstalt said its interests in other companies generally fared very well and that it continued to concentrate on the core business of the bank by pulling out of interests in the non-banking sector.

The integration with Bank Austria is expected to rack up extra costs this year although this should be offset by considerable savings over the coming years, the bank said, adding earnings per share are expected to be substantially higher than the 70 schillings last year.
In late trade Bank Austria's preference shares were trading five schillings higher at 440. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
